case.believed: z.record(z.enum(...), valueSchema) behaves like a normal sparse dictionary: enum members are merely the allowed keys, missing enum keys are accepted, and extra keys fail with the same invalid_key shape as z.partialRecord.
contract: z.record with a z.enum key schema is exhaustive in Zod 4.4.3: every enum member must be present, and a missing member produces invalid_type at that member's path.
An enum-key z.record reports both a wrong present value and every missing enum member in the same safeParse result.
Extra keys on exhaustive enum-key z.record produce one root-level unrecognized_keys issue.
z.partialRecord with the same enum accepts missing members but still rejects an extra key with invalid_key at the extra key path and a nested invalid_value issue listing the enum values.
z.record with z.string keys remains an open sparse dictionary and neither requires enum members nor rejects arbitrary string keys.
case.goal: Prove Zod 4.4.3 exhaustive z.record enum-key validation versus z.partialRecord and open string-key records, including exact missing and extra-key error paths.
